chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the women migrated to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a woman named Umm Habib was among them. She was a 'khafidah' (one who shaves/trim the pubic hair) who would shave the maidservants. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw her, he said to her, 'O Umm Habib, the work that was in your hand is in your hand today.' She said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, unless it is forbidden, in which case you would forbid me from it.' He said, 'No, rather it is permissible. Come closer to me so that I may teach you.' She came closer, and he said to her, 'O Umm Habib, when you do it, do not remove it completely (do not uproot it), and sniff (the area), for it is brighter for the face and more pleasing to the husband.'

Umm Habib had a sister named Umm Attiya, who was a 'muqayyinah' (meaning a hairdresser/comber). When Umm Habib returned to her sister and informed her of what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had said to her, Umm Attiya went to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and informed him of what her sister had told her. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her, 'Come closer to me, O Umm Attiya. When you comb the maidservant, do not wash her face with the cloth, for the cloth takes away the water of the face.'

key_terms.أُمُّ حَبِيب: A companion of the Prophet, known for her grooming skills
key_terms.أُمُّ عَطِيَّة: Sister of Umm Habib, a hairdresser
key_terms.خَافِضَة: A woman who shaves or trims pubic hair
key_terms.مُقَيِّنَة: A hairdresser or one who combs hair

ai.seo_question: What are the specific prophetic instructions regarding personal grooming practices like shaving and hair combing for women?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on professions, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) guidance to female artisans, specifically Umm Habib (the hair-shaver) and Umm Attiya (the hairdresser), validating their trades as lawful livelihoods. The Prophet’s specific advice to avoid 'uprooting' (complete removal) and excessive washing underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining natural beauty and modesty while engaging in professional grooming services.
